parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Gas-liquid chromatography involves a stationary phase and a mobile phase.
parts.text: Name, or describe in detail, a suitable substance that could be used for each phase.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
A mixture of three organic compounds is separated by gas-liquid chromatography. The chromatogram obtained is shown in Fig. 9.1. The amount of each substance is proportional to the area under its peak.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 9.1

Explain the meaning of retention time.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the percentage of B in the mixture. Show your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State the number of peaks that would be seen in the proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of methyl butanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$. Name all the splitting patterns seen in this spectrum.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
D and E are both esters with the molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$. Their proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectra are shown in Fig. 9.2 and Fig. 9.3.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

Fig. 9.2

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

Fig. 9.3

Table 9.2

| environment of proton | example | typical chemical shift range, $\delta$/ppm |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| alkane | $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_2-$, $>\text{CH}-$ | 0.9-1.7 |
| alkyl next to $\text{C=O}$ | $\text{CH}_3-\text{C=O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{C=O}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{C=O}$ | 2.2-3.0 |
| alkyl next to aromatic ring | $\text{CH}_3-\text{Ar}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{Ar}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{Ar}$ | 2.3-3.0 |
| alkyl next to electronegative atom | $\text{CH}_3-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ | 3.2-4.0 |
| attached to alkene | $=\text{CHR}$ | 4.5-6.0 |
parts.text:
Deduce the structures of the two esters D and E and draw their displayed formulae in the boxes below.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
The spectrum of D includes a quartet at $\delta$ 4.1.

Identify the protons responsible for this quartet on your structure in (i) by labelling these protons with the letter F.

Explain why this peak is split into a quartet.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
The spectrum of E has a doublet at $\delta$ 1.1.

Identify the protons responsible for this doublet on your structure in (i) by labelling these protons with the letter G.

Explain why this peak has a chemical shift of 1.1.
